evidence.section: 4.3. Influence of Ti and Ta on oxidation resistance
evidence.quote: The increase in Ti content in the alloy increased the activity of Co, which further induced CoO production (Figs. 3(d), 5(d), and 7(d)) and improved the oxidized weight gain of the alloys.

mechanisms.name: stress from TaO2 growth causing Al2O3 rupture

evidence.section: 4.3. Influence of Ti and Ta on oxidation resistance
evidence.quote: The estimated stress generated by the growth of TaO2 in the Al2O3 layer is ~2.2 GPa [30], which is close to the theoretical compressive strength of the α-Al2O3 layer (~2.6 GPa) [31]. The superposition of thermal stresses can lead to the rupture of the Al2O3 layer, which decreases oxidation resistance and increases the oxidized weight gain of the alloys.
